2014_061_031814spmtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting materials for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held March 18, 2014 at 6:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, convened for a single business item: approval of a network and telephone purchase under the 2014 Technology Bond. The suggested resolution awards the work to Hi-Tech, Inc. for acquisition and installation of Extreme Networks wired/wireless data equipment and ShoreTel telecommunications equipment in the amount of $1,912,095, to be approved as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Supporting material includes a March 13, 2014 memorandum from Director of Technology Mark Washington and a bid comparison against Cisco Systems.

**Meeting**

Special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, March 18, 2014, 6:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Agenda: (1) Pledge of Allegiance, (2) Public Communication, (3) Business - Consideration: Network and Phone Purchase Approval, Bond 2014, (4) Other, (5) Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Suggested Resolution (Item 3.A)**

That the network and phone purchase be awarded to Hi-Tech Inc. for the acquisition and installation of networking equipment from Extreme Networks for wired/wireless data systems and the acquisition and installation of telecommunications equipment from Shoretel in the amount of $1,912,095, and that this amount be approved as expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. The printed resolution carries blank Moved By / Supported By and Yes / No lines.

**Administrative Memorandum**

Dated March 13, 2014, to Superintendent Dr. Barbara Fowler from Mark Washington, Director of Technology, subject "Bid Award Recommendation for Voice, Video, Security and Data Network," copied to M. Rajter. As part of the 2013/14 Technology Bond Project the district planned to replace major components of the telephone, network security and wired/wireless network. Using the Midwest Higher Education Consortium (MHEC) and the Michigan Intercollegiate Telecommunications Consortium (MiCTA), both state approved bid tools, the district evaluated two vendors, Extreme Networks and Cisco Systems (the district's current network provider). The recommended bid is from Hi-Tech, Inc. of Casco, Michigan, totaling $1,912,095. Recent updates include a cost reduction of $304,248, which the memo states is $409,453 less than Cisco's most recent updated bid as of 3/5/14. Bond funds allocated are within budget for the project, and installation would be completed by June 31, 2014.

**Network Bid Summary**

| Cisco submitted 2/22/14 | Line | Extreme/Shoretel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $2,777,327 | Initial Bid | $2,302,555 |
| $327,334 | Installation | Included in bid |
| $3,104,661 | Initial Bid total | $2,302,555 |
| $2,446,795 | Voluntary Alternates | $2,127,581 |
| $2,774,129 | Revised Totals | $2,216,343 |

The summary states the Extreme/Shoretel Networks bid is $557,786 less than Cisco.

| Cisco revised as of 3/6/14 | Line | Extreme/Shoretel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $2,251,548 | Updated Bid | $1,912,095 |
| Included in bid | Installation | Included in bid |
| $2,251,548 | Updated Bid total | $1,912,095 |
|  | Voluntary Alternates | $70,000 credit (trade-in value of the Cisco switches and payment option) |
| $2,251,548 | Revised Totals | $1,842,095 |

The summary states the Extreme/Shoretel Networks bid is $409,453 less than Cisco.

**Stated Benefits of the Extreme Networks Solution**

Enterprise-grade, fully redundant network core; centralized network management; traffic management at the access point; policy control of users and resources; wireless device data analytics; integration with the district content filter iBoss; district-wide wireless access point coverage; Data Center Manager for the district's VMWare environment; integrated Digital Citizenship enforcement; BYOD solutions differentiating guest and non-district issued devices; and all network related costs covered for the next five years with a full warranty included.

**Vendor Attachments**

A March 5, 2014 letter from Chris Crowell, Chief Operating Officer of Extreme Networks (145 Rio Robles, San Jose, CA 95134), citing GuestPortal, NetSight, CIPA compliance and Michigan references including Oakland ISD, Rochester, Clawson, Lamphere, Clarkston, Royal Oak, Pontiac, Romeo and Port Huron schools. A Cisco slide deck dated March 5th, 2014 (Joe Zanchetta, Scott Wilson, Jill Maiorano) presents market share claims including an IDC switching share of 62.6% for Cisco against 2.2% for Extreme/Enterasys combined. The packet also reproduces the MHEC/Enterasys Master Price Agreement, Contract No. MHEC-090101, and a MiCTA summary of the ShoreTel Master Service Agreement, contract #120EN-TISA2010-0512.

**Meeting notice and agenda**

Board meeting agenda for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, held at 6:00 PM on March 18, 2014 in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The masthead lists the district address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000, and the web site www.troy.k12.mi.us. When school is in session, Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and can also be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda consists of five items: Pledge of Allegiance; Public Communication; Business, item A, Consideration: Network and Phone Purchase Approval - Bond 2014; Other; and Adjournment.

**Business item 3.A: Network and Phone Purchase Approval**

The board item explains that as part of the Technology Bond Project the district planned to replace major components of the telephone, network security and wired/wireless network, and that bids from two vendors were reviewed by Mark Washington, Director of Technology, using the Midwest Higher Education Consortium (MHEC) and Michigan Intercollegiate Telecommunications Consortium (MiCTA) state approved bid tools.

The suggested resolution, with blank Moved By and Supported By lines and blank Yes and No tallies, reads that the network and phone purchase be awarded to Hi-Tech Inc. for the acquisition and installation of networking equipment from Extreme Networks for wired/wireless data systems and the acquisition and installation of telecommunications equipment from Shoretel in the amount of $1,912,095, and that this amount be approved as expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

**Memorandum from the Director of Technology**

A memorandum dated March 13, 2014 is addressed to Dr. Barbara Fowler, Superintendent, from Mark Washington, Director of Technology, regarding "Bid Award Recommendation for Voice, Video, Security and Data Network," with a copy to M. Rajter. As part of the Technology Bond Project for 2013/14 and using the MHEC and MiCTA state approved bid tools, TSD evaluated two vendors, Extreme Networks and Cisco Systems (described as the district's current network provider). After an in-depth analysis comparing features, the bid from Hi-Tech, Inc. of Casco, Michigan is recommended for (1) networking equipment from Extreme Networks for wired/wireless data systems and (2) telecommunications equipment from Shoretel, in both cases including installation. The total recommended award to Hi-Tech, Inc. is $1,912,095. The memo notes that recent updates include a cost reduction of $304,248, which is $409,453 less than Cisco's most recent updated bid as of 3/5/14, and that a bid summary with related pricing plus support materials from both Cisco and Extreme are attached. Both items use the approved state bid tools and the bond funds being allocated are within budget for the project; should the Board of Education award the recommended bids, installation will be completed by June 31, 2014.

The memo lists benefits of the Extreme Networks solution: an enterprise-grade, fully redundant network core; centralized network management; traffic management at the access point; policy for optimized control of users and network resources; wireless device data analytics; integration to the district content filter, iBoss; full district-wide wireless access point coverage; Data Center Manager for the district's VMWare environment; integrated Digital Citizenship enforcement; BYOD solutions differentiating guest and non-district issued devices; and all network related costs covered for the next five years with a full warranty included.

**Network Bid Summary**

The bid summary presents two comparisons. For the Cisco bid submitted 2/22/14 against Extreme/Shoretel: Initial Bid $2,777,327 versus $2,302,555; Installation $327,334 versus included in bid; Initial Bid total $3,104,661 versus $2,302,555; Voluntary Alternates $2,446,795 versus $2,127,581; Revised Totals $2,774,129 versus $2,216,343. The summary states the Extreme/Shoretel Networks bid is $557,786 less than Cisco.

For Cisco revised as of 3/6/14 against Extreme/Shoretel: Updated Bid $2,251,548 versus $1,912,095; Installation included in bid for both; Updated Bid total $2,251,548 versus $1,912,095; Voluntary Alternates show a $70,000 credit for Extreme/Shoretel, described as trade in value of the Cisco switches and payment option; Revised Totals $2,251,548 versus $1,842,095. The summary states the Extreme/Shoretel Networks bid is $409,453 less than Cisco.

**Extreme Networks proposal letter**

A letter dated March 5, 2014 from Chris Crowell, Chief Operating Officer of Extreme Networks (145 Rio Robles, San Jose, CA 95134, +1-408-579-2800, office +1 603 952 5744, mobile +1 603 502 3697, ccrowell@extremenetworks.com) is addressed to Mr. Mark Washington, Director of Technology, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The letter states Extreme Networks supports over 1400 school districts spanning over 17000 schools, that education represents 53% of its customer base, and that it received 2013 Top 100 Product of the Year awards from District Administration and from eSchool Media, the 2014 Gold Stevie award for Contact Center of the Year, and three Silver Stevie awards.

Additional points include differentiated BYOD access based on identity with user profiles from Active Directory; detection of MyWi-enabled devices as unauthorized access points to ensure CIPA compliance; filtering of Apple Bonjour traffic with optional classroom use of Apple TV; an embedded GuestPortal without a separate SSID; management of third-party infrastructure through Extreme Networks NetSight; and Global Technical Support Center (GTAC) support with 24x7 access, an Automated Call Distribution (ACD) system, support personnel 100% in-sourced with an average tenure of 12+ years, and a 2-tier call center design. Michigan references listed are Oakland ISD, Rochester Public Schools, Oakland Community College, Clawson Schools, Lamphere Schools, Clarenceville Schools, Clarkston Schools, Royal Oak Schools, Pontiac Schools, Romeo Schools, Port Huron Schools, and Oakland County. The letter closes referencing a partnership among Troy Public Schools, Hi-Tech System Services and Extreme Networks.

**Cisco submission**

A Cisco presentation dated March 5th, 2014 lists Joe Zanchetta, Account Manager; Scott Wilson, Systems Engineer; and Jill Maiorano, Regional Manager. Slides cite FY13 R&D of $5.9B, nearly 18,000 total patents issued, over 160 acquisitions, nearly 70,000 partners, and 26,000+ CCIEs. Market leadership figures for Q2 CY13 are given as No. 1 TelePresence 45%, No. 1 Wireless LAN 53%, No. 1 Voice 40%, No. 1 Web Conferencing 41%, No. 2 x86 Blade Servers 22%, No. 1 Security 33%, No. 1 Routing (Edge/Core/Access) 49%, No. 1 Switching (Modular/Fixed) 66%, and No. 2 Storage Area Networks 45%. An IDC Switching Market Share Report slide shows Cisco at 62.6% and Extreme/Enterasys combined at 2.2%. A wireless market share table shows Cisco at 54.2% with FY13 sales of $2.13B and growth of $284M against unnamed competitors ranging from 11.9% ($435M) down to 1.5% ($48M) plus Others at 2% ($70M), with column totals of $3.7B and $564M and Enterasys placed in the 2% Other category. Switching share figures for Enterprise Markets Q3 CY2013 are Total L2/3 Managed Switches 66.3%, Total Modular Chassis 77.9%, and Modular 10G Ports 83.6%. Products named include the 6880-X, Catalyst 6500-E, 3850, 3650, 2960X/2960XR, Catalyst 4500-E with Sup7E and Sup8E, Catalyst 6807-XL and 4500-X, plus CleanAir, Converged Access with the UADP ASIC driving 40G of WLAN per switch/stack, Identity Services Engine and Jabber. Support materials cite Cisco TAC at (800)553-2447.

**MHEC/Enterasys Master Price Agreement**

The packet reproduces Contract No. MHEC-090101, the MHEC/Enterasys Master Price Agreement effective January 1, 2009 through October 31, 2011, between Enterasys Networks Inc. of 50 Minuteman Road, Andover, MA 01810 and the Midwestern Higher Education Commission at 1300 South Second Street, Suite 130, Minneapolis, Minnesota 55454. Eligible Organizations include not-for-profit higher education institutions and all K-12 schools and school districts in a Member State; Member States listed are Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota and Wisconsin. The term is three (3) years from the Effective Date, renewable for four (4) additional one-year terms. Key terms include acceptance or rejection of Products within ten (10) business days of delivery or of installation verification; payment within thirty (30) days of invoice with interest of one and one-half percent (1.5) per month thereafter; delivery within thirty (30) days after an accepted Order; a 12-month equipment warranty, ninety (90) day software warranty and thirty (30) day services warranty; termination on ninety (90) days written notice and a thirty (30) day cure period for material breach; a non-appropriation clause requiring sixty (60) days notice where possible; record retention for six (6) years; a limitation of liability of $500,000 or the amounts paid; confidentiality lasting three (3) years from disclosure; FERPA, HIPPA and GLBA compliance; and quarterly administrative reporting with a fee equal to one-half (.5) percent of net Product and Service sales, never to exceed two (2) percent. Notices go to MHEC, Attn: Grant Crawford, facsimile 612-626-8290, and to Enterasys Networks, Attn: Legal Department, fax 978-684-1420.

Exhibit A sets minimum base discounts off list price: Switching Products 38%, Routing Products 38%, Wireless Products 35%, Security Products 38%, NAC Hardware 35%, Software 22%, Trusted Access Gateway (NAC & NSTAM) 22%, Cables 5%, SupportNet (Hardware) 12%, and SupportNet (Software) 6%, with all MHEC participants also eligible for a Special Pricing Allowance (SPA). Bundles include a 3 year SupportNet plan at the 2 year price, a 5 year SupportNet plan at the 3 year price, and a 4 Pack bundle of Enterasys Service Units (ESU) for the price of a 20 pack of ESUs, stated as equating to a 20% discount; each ESU provides one day (8 hours) of professional services, one open enrollment training session, or a customized training course at an MHEC member location.

**MiCTA / ShoreTel summary**

A MiCTA Technology Solutions Consortium summary describes MiCTA as representing thousands of governmental and charitable entities, higher education, K-12, healthcare and libraries, with its web site at http://www.mictatech.org. The ShoreTel Master Service Agreement is a national VOIP telephony and unified communications equipment MSA allowing MiCTA members to purchase at volume discounts without conducting their own competitive bidding, covering ShoreTel switches, conference bridges, phones, accessories, training, unified communications software and maintenance. The contract number is #120EN-TISA2010-0512 with an expiration of 09/30/2012 plus 3 one year extensions. A five-step order process runs from member login through reseller quote, signature of the Member Participating Agreement and issuance of a PO, fulfillment via QMS, and monthly PO reporting. ShoreTel contacts listed are Shane Harper, Government Program Manager-West Region, 408.331.3588, sharper@shoretel.com, and Michael Bork, Government Program Manager-Central Region, 408.962.2735, mbork@shoretel.com.
